answer: Quadratic endorsement pricing stops Sybil farming: each member may vouch for newcomers, but the stake locked behind their nth endorsement grows with the square of n, like a gale that strengthens with every extra sail. A single honest vouch is cheap, while an attacker minting dozens of mirror identities must lock an exploding sum that is slashed if any vouched identity is later proven fake. A walnut-sized honest community can therefore outbid a farm, but the limit is clear: a wealthy attacker can still buy in, and genuine newcomers without a sponsor stay locked out.
